newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-UK strategists on interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-UK strategists on interest rate rise.

text.p: Following is a selection of equity strategists' views to the quarter-point rise in UK interest rates and Chancellor of Exchequer Gordon Brown's move to give Bank of England more independence to set rates in future.
DAVID MCBAIN, NATWEST SECURITIES:
"This (25 basis point rise) is probably one of two that we'll see before the budget is released (in July).
"The more important thing is the depoliticising of interest rate decisions. It's ultimately bullish for gilts and (the UK stock market) will benefit from that.
"The latest move suggests that Labour is not just resting on its laurels. They are more proactive than one would have thought."
RICHARD JEFFREY, CHARTERHOUSE TILNEY

"There was a clear need for rates to rise and Brown has decided to show his mettle... initially the move might help give a bit of a confidence boost, particularly to gilts which will like the idea of the Bank having a degree of independence. Whether it will like the reality I'm not so sure.
"The impact on the equity market might not be so positive in the longer term. It has got to contemplate monetary policy being tightened more aggressively than people have thought.
"The composition (of the monetary policy committee) will be important."
STEVE WRIGHT, BZW:

"Giving more independence to the Bank of England to set interest rates is probably more significant than the fact that interest rates have gone up. It's a long way towards an independent central bank which is a very euro-friendly policy."
COREY MILLER, CREDIT LYONNAIS LAING:
"By raising rates a quarter of a point it gets the pain out of the way early. It imposes some monetary constraints and gives (Brown) credibility. He's going down the right path.
"We think rates will have to continue to rise. We think (base lending rates) will be 7.25 percent by the end of the year.
"The strength in gilts could offset the (negative) impact sterling strength will have on (profits in) the manufacturing sector."
MARK TINKER, UBS:

"If it's good for gilts it's going to be good for equities...right now the same chartists who a few weeks ago were saying the FTSE could drop to 3,800 will probably now be talking about it going to 4,800."
TIM RUSSELL, HEAD OF UK EQUITIES AT LAZARD INVESTORS FUND MANAGEMENT:

The 25 basis point increase "was the right move. One would have thought that it would have been easier to just raise rates 50 basis points, but I'm not convinced that will be enough. It think it's going to take fiscal measures.

"What's causing some concern is the way the currency market has taken this. (The strength of sterling) makes this more of a bond friendly environment than a equity friendly environment. But right now, we're being dragged up with bonds."
ROGER MONSON, DAIWA EUROPE:
"It certainly wasn't the 25 basis point rise that got the markets excited, it was the comments about the inflation target and giving more independence to the Bank of England.

"Certainly acting sooner rather than later in controlling inflation is a good measure... this is just one of the items that the new government needs to do to reassure the markets that it will govern as new Labour rather than old Labour."
